problems.title: Cotangents are paired with the wrong edges
claim: The retained ARAP assembly assigns each cotangent to its opposite edge.
analysis: The current official supplemental PatchARAPLoss lists edges \((0,1),(1,2),(0,2)\), but assigns cotangents of angles at vertices \(0,1,2\) in that order rather than to opposite edges. For vertices \((0,0,0),(2,0,0),(0,1,0)\), the angle cotangents are \(0,2,1/2\). Correct edge weights are \(w_{01}=1/2,w_{12}=0,w_{02}=2\); the source gives \(0,2,1/2\). With identity rotations and displacement \((0,0.2,0)\) only at the third vertex, the implemented energy is \(0.10\), becoming \(0.02\) after reversing vertex order without changing geometry. Correct assembly gives \(0.08\) in both orders. No global coefficient removes this ordering dependence; its benchmark effect remains unknown.
result: The bounded local discrepancy or counterexample is supported; no change in published benchmark scores is quantified.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Reconcile the specific equation, reported quantity or source contract described above. Corrected full-experiment results remain unverified.

problems.title: Shared edges are overwritten and counted twice
claim: Shared-edge weights are accumulated and used with the intended multiplicity.
analysis: The current supplemental source assigns all per-face cotangents into a dense matrix using repeated indices, then adds its transpose; it does not scatter-add same-direction contributions. Even after repairing the preceding angle pairing, vertices \[(0,0),(2,0),(0.4,1),(2,2)\] and faces \((0,1,2),(1,3,2)\) give opposite-angle contributions \(0.4\) and \(0.625\) on shared edge \(\{1,2\}\). Their sum must be \(1.025\), while a last-write interpretation gives \(0.625\); cyclically rewriting the second face as \((3,2,1)\) changes the stored result without changing its geometry. GPU repeated-index assignment order was not measured. The later per-face edge list also repeats interior edges, changing their relative contribution after weights have already been assembled. Neither a global sum/mean convention nor a global loss coefficient repairs these relative differences.

problems.title: Approximate-SDF projection need not converge
claim: Repeated normalized-gradient projection converges for the stated approximate fields.
analysis: For \(f(x,y,z)=az\), normalized-gradient iteration gives \(z_{\rm next}=(1-a)z\), converging only for \(0<a<2\). At \(a=2\) it cycles; \(a=3\) diverges. The local exact-SDF interpretation is not refuted.
result: This is a scope/provenance gap, not proof that the stronger empirical conclusion is false.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.

problems.title: Default settings do not identify the reported runs
claim: Default release configuration identifies the stated experimental network and schedule.
analysis: The current final supplementary demo uses invertible width \(128\), versus the paper’s stated \(256\), ARAP weight \(10\) versus the implicit-field setting \(1000\), and an SDF learning-rate milestone override of \(10000\) versus the stated \(1000,2000,5000\). The final README explicitly permits CLI overrides, so these do not establish which settings produced the tables. The separate current public repository is an earlier July 2025 release: its SDF demo already uses ARAP weight \(1000\), although other defaults differ. Thus the weight discrepancy is specifically against the current final supplementary demo, not every author resource. The separate eight-layer, width-\(256\) SDF architecture matches and is not confused with invertible deformation width.

problems.title: Constant optimization cost is not constant total cost
claim: Given a fixed neural field and patch budget, the deformation optimization avoids direct dependence on input mesh vertex count.
analysis: The current high-resolution section explicitly discusses the deformation procedure separately from internal SDF fitting, and Table 4 includes the fitting contribution while Figure 18 excludes it. With a fixed field, patch count and optimization budget, that limited optimization-scaling claim can hold. Producing all \(N\) deformed vertices still costs at least \(\Omega(N)\) time/output space, and field preparation has its own accuracy-dependent cost. This bounds the scope of the claimed stage-level efficiency rather than refuting it as a total-pipeline theorem.
result: The output-size lower bound does not contradict the explicitly scoped optimization comparison; no separate current complexity error is established.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: The current section distinguishes optimization and SDF fitting; a stronger constant total-input/output claim is not required for the reported stage comparison.
problems.existing_correction_status: No repair of the scoped fixed-budget optimization statement follows; end-to-end costs remain separate context.

problems.title: An auxiliary unchanged-vertex test reduces the wrong axis
claim: The auxiliary unchanged-vertex test requires all coordinates to remain fixed.
analysis: The ARAPMesh helper treats any coordinate fixed across neighbors as a wholly unchanged vertex. A planar \(90^\circ\) rotation preserves \(z\) but changes \(x,y\), so affected vertices can be incorrectly zeroed. Main-table impact is unknown.
